chunks: From him, from Ibn Jamhur, from Suleyman ibn Sama' Sama'ah, from Abdul Malik ibn Bahr, raising it, similar to that, and there is an increase in it,
When he bows, he crouches, and when he prostrates, he pecks, and when he sits, he rests on his heels.

key_terms.رَبَضَ: He crouched or sat back on his heels
key_terms.شَغَرَ: He rested on his heels (sitting on the heels for tashahhud)
key_terms.نَقَرَ: He pecked (like a bird), indicating a quick, firm placement of the forehead

ai.seo_question: What are the specific physical postures described for bowing, prostrating, and sitting in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* elaborates on the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) physical etiquette (*adab*) in prayer, specifically highlighting the distinct postures of *rabada* (sitting back on heels) during bowing, *naqara* (pecking with the forehead) during prostration, and *shaghara* (spreading fingers) during sitting. These details underscore the Shia emphasis on replicating the Sunnah’s precise bodily movements to embody humility and presence of heart (*khushu*) in worship.
